motivation.text: The source transform length and the target length are coprime, so the Fourier transform of one length must be moved onto the power-of-two frequencies of the other; Gaussian weights move between the two sets of frequencies.

adds.name: near-identity factor
adds.meaning: The map $N=CTD$, which is the identity up to a Gaussian error of norm below one half.

adds.name: coordinate selection
adds.meaning: The map that selects the coordinates $q_j$ nearest to $tj/s$ from a vector of length $t$.

adds.name: Gaussian phase
adds.meaning: The diagonal map that multiplies coordinate $j$ by $e^{\pi\alpha^2\beta_j^2}$ to cancel the Gaussian factor at the selected coordinate.

adds.name: input contraction
adds.meaning: The linear contraction $A:\mathbb{C}^s\to\mathbb{C}^t$ that the identity applies before the target transform.

adds.name: output contraction
adds.meaning: The linear contraction $B_0:\mathbb{C}^t\to\mathbb{C}^s$ that the identity applies after the target transform.
